harmonicFunction: Em9 (i9) - Minor tonic chord enriched with the major 9th (F#) for a lush, open modern rock texture
Cadd9 (bVIadd9) - Submediant chord providing emotional optimism and bright upper harmonics
A7sus4 (IV7sus4) - Subdominant chord introducing the Dorian raised 6th (C#) for signature sophistication
Cmaj7 (bVImaj7) - Major seventh color providing smooth voice leading back to Em9

techniques.name: Syncopated Acoustic 16th-Note Funk Strum
techniques.description: Mike Einziger's groovy rhythm: continuous 16th-note pendulum right hand, combined with percussive left-hand fret-hand mutes (chucks) and quick chord slides

sequence: Keep right wrist loose in steady 16th-note down-up pendulum motion
Fret Em9 cleanly and slide into Cadd9 with light pressure
Release left-hand finger pressure on unaccented 16ths to create percussive chucks
Accent the upbeat 'and' of beat 2 and beat 4
tips: Relax your fret hand — the percussive sound comes from relaxing finger pressure, not hitting strings harder
Let the high open strings ring on the chord hits to create the signature spacious atmosphere
Keep the 90 BPM groove tight with a clean metronome

sections.name: Intro
sections.description: Mike Einziger establishes the groovy, syncopated acoustic motif that defines the song.
notes: Notice the sweet major 9th note (F#) in Em9
Percussive fret-hand mutes between chord hits

sections.name: Verse
sections.description: Brandon Boyd's philosophical vocals float over the syncopated extended chord progression.
sections.progression: Em9 - Cadd9 - A7sus4 - Cmaj7 - Em9 - Cadd9 - A7sus4 - Cmaj7
notes: Maintain relaxed wrist motion without rushing
Hit the bass notes clearly on beat 1
Let the open treble strings chime

sections.name: Chorus
sections.description: The soaring chorus hook with expanded acoustic strumming and dynamic vocal delivery.
notes: Fuller dynamic stroke on the downbeats
Sing the uplifting hook with emotional conviction
Clean slide into the post-chorus groove

sections.name: Scale Practice Exercise
sections.description: Scale exercise highlighting the C natural (Aeolian) to C# (Dorian) melodic shift.
notes: Notice how C# on string 2 fret 2 injects the bright Dorian color
Connect scale notes directly to the Em9 and A7sus4 shapes

beginner.title: Master the Extended Chord Voicings
steps: Learn the open shapes for Em9 (0-2-2-0-3-2) and Cadd9 (X-3-2-0-3-0)
Strum through the 4-chord progression at 70 BPM

intermediate.title: Master the Syncopated 16th-Note Chuck
steps: Incorporate left-hand fret mutes (chucks) between chord hits
Work on the up-the-neck jazz voicings used on the record
Lock into the 90 BPM groove with a metronome

advanced.title: Full Acoustic Performance & Soloing
steps: Incorporate Mike Einziger's acoustic solo using E minor pentatonic
Sing lead vocals while executing the syncopated rhythm
Deliver an effortless, groovy acoustic interpretation

commonMistakes: Stiff right wrist — the 16th-note strum must feel loose and funky
Hitting the 6th string during the Cadd9 chord (keep 6th string muted with thumb tip)
practiceRoutine: 5 minutes: Percussive strumming drill on muted strings
5 minutes: Main progression (Em9 - Cadd9 - A7sus4 - Cmaj7) at 90 BPM
5 minutes: Chorus singing and playing integration
metronomeWork: Practice at 75 BPM to lock in the 16th-note syncopations
Advance to target 90 BPM once chord transitions are automatic
Set metronome on beats 2 and 4 to internalize the backbeat pocket
